full_judgment: 4. In Writ Petition No. 346/91 the petitioner Abdul Gani stated that he opened the letter of credit on 10.5.88 when the existing notification, namely, SRO 114 dated 18.6.87 provided sales tax at 10%, SRO 115 dated 18.6.87 providing tariff value at Taka 15,000.00 per metric ton and statutory rate of duty on import tariff value was fixed at 50%. The goods arrived at Chittagong port on 9.8.88. It is stated that SRO. 142 dated 16.6.88, 143 dated 16.6.88 and 144 dated 16.6.88 were issued by the Ministry of Finance raising the tariff value, sale tax in respect of the aforesaid goods. The petitioner submitted 3 bills of entry on 29.1.90 provisionally. The Customs have assessed the duty and sales tax at an enhanced rate on the basis of the SRO 192 dated 15.6.89, 193 dated 15.6.89 and 188 dated 15.6.89 and realised duty and taxes on 6.6.90. It is stated that the petitioner had invested considerable amount of money finding the high demand of the said goods in the local market at the time of opening the L/C. The Government did not pay any heed to the demand of the petitioner as such the petitioner moved this application and obtained the present Rule.
